fullPassage: Everyone loves getting something for free, and these days it is easier than ever to receive a variety of free items. Companies give away free food, free T-shirts, even free cell phones. This might not seem like a smart thing for businesses to do, but it’s actually a well-planned strategy based on something called “freeconomics.” One basic practice of freeconomics is letting people try something once in order to make them become regular customers. For example, if you are given a free coffee at a café one morning, you might come back day after day to buy the same drink. This is the same reason a company might send you a small container of shampoo in the mail—they hope you will buy a full bottle the next time you go shopping. Another strategy of freeconomics is to give consumers something for free, knowing they will then need to purchase something to accompany it. A phone company, for example, may give you a free cell phone, but you then need to pay for an annual plan. The concept of freeconomics has been around for a while, but the Internet has made it more popular than ever. Because the cost of running an online business is so low, websites are constantly offering free benefits in the hope of attracting more visitors. Although some people will simply take advantage of the free offerings, the business may be able to convince them to upgrade to more attractive paid services. This is known as the “freemium” strategy, a combination of the words “free” and “premium.” Some experts believe freeconomics will eventually change the way business takes place. Already, any company with a superior product can benefit by giving potential consumers a free taste. And online, there are plenty of businesses, such as YouTube and Google, that don’t need to sell anything to consumers at all. They simply attract millions of people to their websites with free services, and then they make their profits from charging other companies to advertise on their site. These businesses make money, and we get to enjoy something for free.

Companies give away free food, free T-shirts, even free cell phones. This might not seem like a smart thing for businesses to do, but it’s actually a well-planned strategy based on something called “freeconomics.” One basic practice of freeconomics is letting people try something once in order to make them become regular customers. For example, if you are given a free coffee at a café one morning, you might come back day after day to buy the same drink. This is the same reason a company might send you a small container of shampoo in the mail—they hope you will buy a full bottle the next time you go shopping. Another strategy of freeconomics is to give consumers something for free, knowing they will then need to <u>purchase</u> something to accompany it. A phone company, for example, may give you a free cell phone, but you then need to pay for an annual plan. The concept of freeconomics has been around for a while, but the Internet has made it more popular than ever. Because the cost of running an online business is so low, websites are constantly offering free benefits in the hope of attracting more visitors. Although some people will simply take advantage of the free offerings, the business may be able to convince them to upgrade to more attractive paid services. This is known as the “freemium” strategy, a combination of the words “free” and “premium.” Some experts believe freeconomics will eventually change the way business takes place. Already, any company with a superior product can benefit by giving potential consumers a free taste. And online, there are plenty of businesses, such as YouTube and Google, that don’t need to sell anything to consumers at all. They simply attract millions of people to their websites with free services, and then they make their profits from charging other companies to advertise on their site. These businesses make money, and we get to enjoy something for free.

questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 free의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: free: (A) 무료의 (B) 자유로운
det.analysis:
① (A) 자유로운 (B) 무료의: 순서가 반대예요

② (A) 무료의 (B) 한가한: (B)는 '자유로운'이에요

③ (A) 무료의 (B) 자유로운: 쿠폰으로 '무료로' 받다 + 의견을 낼 '자유가 있다' ←정답

④ (A) 여유로운 (B) 자유로운: (A)는 '무료의'예요
det.tip: coffee for free = 무료 vs free to express = 자유로운.

③ investor: 투자자 — 정의와 달라요

det.tip: a person who buys goods → 소비자(consumer).

questions.passage: The concept of freeconomics has been around for a while, but the Internet has made it more popular than ever. Because the cost of running an online business is so low, websites are constantly __________ (offer) free benefits in the hope of attracting more visitors.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: offer → offering: 'are constantly __________'는 현재진행형이라 현재분사(-ing)로 바꿔요.
det.analysis:
'websites are constantly __________'에서 be동사(are) 뒤라 현재진행형이에요. 웹사이트가 무료 혜택을 계속 '제공하고 있는' 것이니 offer를 offering으로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 offer를 offering으로 써요.

questions.passage: Some experts believe freeconomics will eventually change the way business takes place. Already, any company with a superior product can benefit by __________ (give) potential consumers a free taste.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: give → giving: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 써요.
det.analysis:
'can benefit by __________'에서 전치사 by 뒤라 동명사가 와야 해요. '~을 줌으로써' 이득을 본다는 뜻이라 give를 동명사 giving으로 바꿔요.

→ 따라서 give를 giving으로 써요.
